rules.label: ASE
rules.words: Auto exhibits are most often aligned with ASE cert titles and I started adding those to later exhibit titles in parens after the title
rules.tip: An automotive exhibit named for an ASE test takes the test's official name, then its code in parentheses: Medium/Heavy Truck Parts Specialist (ASE P1). The program name does not lead (Sam, 2026-11-11). A title already under an older form waits in the rename batch.

ruling.words: Use the cert's official name first and the code in parentheses: "Medium/Heavy Truck Parts Specialist (ASE P1)". Don't put the program name in front, so "Automotive Technology (...)" is out. Students search by the cert name, and colleges adopt by it.

notes: Why a noncredit course with a certification's title can qualify for CPL. There are three paths.
Credit by exam, mirrored: credit and noncredit faculty agree on the assessment evidence, and the student is registered in the mirrored credit course and gets a grade.
Credit by exam, not mirrored: the student gets a CX CPL notation and a grade on the credit course.
Industry certification: the student earns the certification, possibly after the noncredit course, and gets credit through an existing articulation.
All three point to the same canonical certification title, so a cert-named noncredit title folds under the certification, not under the program.

rules.label: Numerals
rules.words: Many exhibits use I, II, III and I skipped adjusting some of those to 1,2,3 for consistency.
rules.tip: Roman level numerals become 1, 2, 3. Official names that carry them, such as Firefighter I, keep them.

rules.label: Language level
rules.words: look for beginning labels that should be elementary (our canonical term for 1,2 or 1A,1B and intermediate should be often 2,3 or 2A,2B
rules.tip: A world-language course is Elementary or Intermediate, then the language, then 1 or 2: Elementary Spanish 1, Intermediate Spanish 2.

rules.label: Course number
rules.words: Looks for any exhibits where I didn't take off the local course number
rules.tip: The canonical title still carries a college's course number or a method word such as Credit by Exam.

rules.label: Level differs
rules.words: exhibits that look the same but still have differences
rules.tip: The local title names one level (1A, Year 5, Level 2) and its canonical title another. Often a title accepted with its neighbor's name.

rules.label: Fold
rules.words: Compare to all the exhibit titles in the whole data set and let's see if we can take another sweep through to adjust and fold
rules.tip: Two canonical titles that differ only in spelling, one title over different courses at one college, or a family whose level word sits in two places.
